title: Future generations
summary: People who don't exist yet can't vote, complain, or say thank you. How much do you owe them?
intro: Every choice about resources, debt, and the climate trades off between people alive today and people who will be born long after you're gone.

questions.prompt: How much should today's generation sacrifice — lower consumption, higher taxes — to leave more resources for people 100 years from now?
A popular program would help millions today, paid for by debt that will still be owed by people not yet born.

options.label: Fund it — help people who need it now
Do a smaller version that doesn't require future debt
Pay for it now, even if that means doing less

questions.prompt: A policy would prevent a disaster in 200 years that would harm millions who don't exist yet, at a real cost to people alive now.

options.label: No — we can't sacrifice real people for hypothetical ones
Pay some of the cost, but not at the expense of people alive today
Pay the cost now — their lives will matter just as much as ours

questions.prompt: Would it be better for the world to have far fewer people living excellent lives, or far more people living merely decent ones?
A regulation would cut everyone's consumption choices today — what you can buy, how you travel — to protect the climate for future generations.

options.label: Leave it voluntary — people should choose for themselves

questions.prompt: How small a benefit today would justify a policy that adds even a tiny chance of contributing to human extinction centuries from now?
questions.noneLabel: No benefit justifies any added extinction risk
